extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy Voting and Professional Members, media companies, and entrants submitting recordings for GRAMMY consideration
extracted.subtask_description: Official rules and screening/guideline criteria for submitting recordings, albums, and related works to the 67th GRAMMY Awards, and for how entries are screened, nominated, and judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Period
rubrics_metrics.description: The 67th GRAMMY Awards eligibility period is Sept. 16, 2023 - Aug. 30, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings must be released during this period and be commercially released, nationally distributed and available from any date within the eligibility period through at least the date of the current year’s Final Round voting deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Recordings (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "New recordings" is defined as material that has been recorded within five years of the release date and not previously released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings not newly recorded are only eligible in specified categories (e.g., Best Historical Album, Best Compilation Soundtrack Album, Best Immersive Audio Album if mix is new, Best Remixed Recording if remix is new, Best Recording Package if package is new, Best Special Package if package is new, Best Album Notes if notes are new, certain classical multidisc sets under stated conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: "General distribution" is defined as the broad release of a recording, available nationwide via brick-and-mortar stores, third-party online retailers and/or streaming services. (Imports are not eligible.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All recordings entered must have an assigned ISRC or UPC number. The Academy may request documentation (list of retailers/streaming services) to verify distribution or release date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Streaming Services
rubrics_metrics.description: "Streaming services" is defined as paid subscription, full catalog, on-demand streaming/limited download services that have existed as such within the United States for at least one full year as of the entry deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spoken word albums are not typically available for streaming; exceptions (e.g., SoundCloud, e-reader site links) may be allowed for those entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings Availability Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings must be available to the public as stand-alone, audio-only purchases or streams (exceptions: opera, immersive audio album and music video/music film) beginning on any date within the eligibility year to be GRAMMY-eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-Edition Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited-edition releases do not meet the distribution requirement for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution eligibility is based on an artist’s typical shipment policies; the Academy may inquire about shipment quantities and determine eligibility if shipments are substantially less than normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Recordings Technical Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering and Producer entries require the submission of a lossless streaming link; if not available, the original digital file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original digital file and the product sent must have quality comparable to at least 16 bit 44.1 kHz (and 44 kHz/16 bit audio for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical and Best Engineered Album, Classical). Include a copy of label credits in required metadata; provide requested documentation if asked by the Academy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized (Non-infringing) Recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings must be non-infringing, original works of authorship; appropriate authorization must be obtained for any third-party copyrighted work embodied in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allegations are made that a recording is unauthorized, the Academy will consider those allegations and determine eligibility in its sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singles and Tracks Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A single is a song released separately; a track is an individual song released as part of an album. Tracks and singles are judged identically in Categories where both are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A track or single from a previous year’s album may be eligible provided it was not entered previously and the album did not win a GRAMMY in a performance Category; various category-specific exclusions apply (e.g., certain composition and craft categories). A track released as a single in another year may be eligible separately for music video etc., in their respective years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An album is a collection of audio recordings issued as a unit and must contain at least five tracks (different songs, not different mixes) and have a total playing time of at least 15 minutes, or may have any number of tracks if the total playing time is at least 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated, revised or expanded versions of previously submitted albums will not be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Newly Recorded Playing Time Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Albums must contain greater than 75% playing time of newly recorded (within five years of release date), previously unreleased recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible in a specific Genre Category, an album must contain greater than 50% playing time of the genre specified by the Field. A recording may not be in more than one specialized Genre Field, though album and track placements may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured Artist Recognition Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized as a GRAMMY nominee, a featured artist must be credited as a featured artist and make a significant and artistic contribution beyond accompaniment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured Artists are award-eligible in genre album Categories if they perform greater than 50% of playing time; in performance Categories if credited as a featured artist on the track/single. Featured artists performing under 50% of a winning album receive a Winners Certificate. Determination whether an album is a 'Various Artists' recording is made case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Mixes and Remixes Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one version/mix of a recording is eligible in the GRAMMY process in any year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different versions are released in the same eligibility year, the label releasing the original artist’s version decides which mix to enter (provided chosen mix is eligible). Remixes/alternate mixes of recordings released in a previous awards year are only eligible in Best Remixed Recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampled and Interpolated Material
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample is an element of a previously released recording incorporated into a new recording. Recordings featuring samples/interpolations are eligible in performance Categories only if the performance is newly recorded per Academy definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings featuring samples are eligible in songwriting Categories, but writers of sampled/interpolated material are not considered nominees or recipients for the portion that consists of such sampled material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative Artificial Intelligence (A.I.) Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only human creators are eligible to be submitted for consideration for, nominated for, or win a GRAMMY Award; a work with no human authorship is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work that features A.I. material is eligible only if (1) the human authorship component is meaningful and more than de minimis; (2) that human authorship is relevant to the Category; and (3) authors of any A.I. material are not eligible to be nominees or recipients for the portion that consists of such A.I. material. The Academy may disqualify entries lacking meaningful human authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: De Minimis Definition (in context of A.I.)
rubrics_metrics.description: De minimis is defined as lacking significance or importance; so minor as to merit disregard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voices Used as 'Instruments' Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocal performances are never eligible as instrumental performances, regardless of method of vocal production (scatting, beatboxing, throat singing, or vocally mimicking instruments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings Released by the Recording Academy or Telecast Recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings released by the Recording Academy or affiliate-produced releases, including releases of performances from GRAMMY Awards Telecasts, are not eligible in the awards process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Recordings Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Student recordings are eligible if they meet all other eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playback Systems Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a specialized piece of equipment is needed to play a recording (other than common consumer devices), the recording is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Pianocorder cassettes are not eligible because they only play back on a Pianocorder system retrofit onto a piano.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings Made of Playback Systems Using Previously Recorded Performances
rubrics_metrics.description: A new recording that records a device playing a previously 'recorded' performance (e.g., piano rolls, player piano systems, Zenph players) is not eligible in the Best Historical Album Category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These playback-system recordings may be eligible in Best Engineered Album, where the new recording of the playback would be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For song lyrics or album notes originally written in one language and translated or adapted into another for release, the original writer is always the eligible writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Screening Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are screened by committees of genre experts to determine appropriate Category and Field placement from time entries are first received until the first ballot is finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening Committees should consider the artist’s intent (as indicated by the Category initially entered); if unsure, artist intent should be the deciding factor. There is a National Screening Committee for Best New Artist and unresolved screening issues; many separate genre Screening Committees exist (list provided). Comedy Album entries are screened by staff and, if necessary, by consultation with experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy Rights and Disqualification Powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy reserves rights including disqualifying entries for incorrect/incomplete information, missing required product, rule violations, placing selections into Categories it deems appropriate, designating classification of achievement, making final determinations of persons entitled to awards recognition, and taking measures to protect integrity from outside influence or bloc voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy can withdraw Categories for insufficient entries, disqualify excessive entries, require submitters to review lists prior to final submission, and remove entries violating Voting and Solicitation Guidelines or website FYC guidelines. Participation in OEP does not guarantee nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Enter (Eligibility to Submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Voting and Professional Recording Academy Members and registered media companies that release eligible recordings during the eligibility period may make GRAMMY entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy reserves the right to remove entries where the submitter is not an individual who would be entitled to receive a nomination or statuette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Fees and Media Company Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Media companies pay an annual registration fee 20% more than individuals; fee is $180 for the 67th GRAMMY Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Fees and Courtesy Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The per-entry fee structure: Professional and Voting Members receive five (5) courtesy entries annually; after that, fees apply. Fee waiver requests may be made for hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early/standard/final pricing tiers exist for Members and Media Companies (specific dollar amounts set for each period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Limits (system-enforced)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Online Entry Process limits entries such that it 1) limits entries in genre Categories (excluding General Field and Craft Categories) to one per recording for albums; and 2) limits track/single entries to one for performance Categories and one for song/composition Categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries Are Made for Specific Recordings (UPC/ISRC requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry requires the UPC or ISRC for the recording being submitted, upload and confirmation of full track listing and confirmed final crediting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrant affirms the specific recorded version should be used by Screening and Craft Committees and for GRAMMY voters' streaming for two rounds. Alternate versions/configurations with different UPC/ISRC and different tracks/credits are not considered for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Nominations and Category Minimum Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: General Field (Record, Song, Album, Best New Artist) nominations = eight; Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical and Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical = five; other Categories = five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In event of tie, nominations no more than seven and no less than three. Each Category must have at least 40 distinct artist entries for full nominations. If 25–39 entries: only three nominations; <25 entries: Category goes on hiatus for the year; <25 entries for three consecutive years -> Category discontinued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry List — Type/Font Treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants may use special characters and unusual typographical treatments in artist names and titles on ballot entry lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters allowed so long as they may be found on a computer keyboard or through standard diacritical markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming Requirements for Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Academy members and media companies must provide several eligible streaming links for each entry (exceptions for certain Craft Categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A variety of streaming links is recommended; if required streaming link or retail-ready product is not received by deadline, the entry may be disqualified. Specific Craft Categories have product submission requirements and exceptions (see product counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Submission Requirements for Certain Craft Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Categories require physical product copies if streaming link not provided: e.g., Best Album Notes (1 copy), Best Immersive Audio Album (3 copies), Best Recording Package (5 copies), Best Historical Album (3 copies), Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical (4 copies if lossless link not submitted), Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical (2 copies if lossless link not submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entry is made in multiple Craft Categories, additional copies must be sent per additional Category. A packing list is generated upon completion of online entries; entrants advised to send a copy with product immediately to the Recording Academy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating Process — Voter Ballot Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are determined by Voting Members through first round voting or Craft Nominating Committee processes. All Voting Members are encouraged to vote in the six Categories of the General Field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voters may vote in up to 10 other Categories on both ballots; the 10 additional Categories must be within no more than three Fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Nominating Committee Eligibility and Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft Committee members must be Voting Members in the membership class corresponding to the Craft they judge and must fill out a Documentation Form listing six tracks or albums for which they have the nomination-eligible credit released in the previous five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form remains on file for five years. Committees are populated via Chapter recommendations, possible CEO/National Chair supplementation for DEI/balance, and ratified by the National Board of Trustees. No person serves more than five consecutive years without a break; chairs may serve additional limited terms as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Committee Composition and Turnover Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee population and term limits: members may serve maximum consecutive years (specific rules vary by committee), at least 25% of each committee must turn over from previous year, committee chairs have separate term rules (examples: members serve five years on and one year off; chairs three years on and two years off).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary to process, committee membership and chair appointments involve confidential votes and ratification steps described in the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Engineered Album — Judging Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic criterion for judging should be the finished product (commercially released recording); overall mix, any unique techniques, quality of sound, and trueness of its reproduction are considered; other factors (e.g., overdubbing, number of tracks, site/mode of recordings) are secondary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligible credited recording engineers, mixers and mastering engineers on a newly recorded non-classical album released during eligibility year are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Of The Year, Classical — Entry and Body-of-Work Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: This Category recognizes excellence in production of classical audio recordings for a producer whose body of work released during the eligibility year represents consistently outstanding creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One album is required to qualify. The body of work will be up to nine projects; if more than nine, the producer selects which nine to include. Minimum qualifications may combine solo and team credits; a producer team must enter projects they worked on as a team; an individual cannot appear both solo and as a member of a producer team on the ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Immersive Audio Album — Eligibility and Mix Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in multichannel immersive audio recordings; eligible recordings must be commercially released on a consumer format/configuration that provides an original immersive mix (not electronically repurposed) of four or more channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On releases with multiple distinct mixes, entrants choose which immersive mix they are entering; only one mix per album will be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Instrumental Composition — Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizes excellence in instrumental composition and is open to any original non-classical composition without lyrics first released on a recording during the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes original instrumental themes/main titles for motion pictures/TV, jazz compositions and new composition backing spoken word entries; instrumental compositions with 'vocal coloring' are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Arrangement (Instrumental or A Cappella) — Definition and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An arrangement is the organization of structure, rhythm, melodies, and harmonies for instruments and/or voices into a cohesive performance; arrangements can be development, enhanced adaptation, or considerable reworking of an original composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category is open to singles/tracks released during eligibility year. No arranger may be entered more than twice in the same arranging Category for arrangements accompanying the same artist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Recording Package / Boxed/Special Package — Screening Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: These Categories recognize excellence in art and packaging for albums, singles, boxed sets or special/limited-edition releases released for the first time during the eligibility year; packaging must be predominantly new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If album art/packaging has been previously released or is a reissue with only minimal new design elements, it is not eligible. Limited-edition and special package releases must still meet general distribution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Album Notes — Screening Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This Category recognizes excellence in album notes writing. Entries must be one piece of original writing written for a specific album and released as part of that album for the first time during the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible notes must be of literary excellence, originality and communicativeness and provide relevant exposition of recorded content. Notes taken from previously issued books/articles/reviews, testimonials, transcripts of prior interviews, or brief letters of praise are not eligible. Books/booklets simultaneously released separately do qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Historical Album — Screening Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in newly created albums featuring historically significant material with new annotation and new packaging that provide important contributions to historical perspective, program content, technology and (where relevant) quality remastering/audio restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible entries may include previously released recordings, alternate takes and/or previously unreleased recordings. Straight reissues with no quality restoration or remastering and no changes in sequence or package are not eligible. Up to three compilation producers can be entered per album.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical Field — Tracks vs Albums Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Categories in the Classical Field accept albums and tracks. If the entire album qualifies as an entry, then tracks from that album are not also eligible in that Category; classical tracks (newly recorded) are allowed entry as separate entities regardless of percentage of playing time of the album.
